pages.title: Alphabet, vowels & spelling
pages.summary: Letters and their final forms, vowel points, the dot that changes b/v k/ch p/f, and modern 'full' spelling. Plus where the keys are.

pages.title: Reading cursive
pages.summary: The handwritten alphabet, the letters that look nothing like print, confusable pairs, and practice notes.

pages.title: Nouns: gender & plural
pages.summary: Masculine or feminine, -im and -ot, pairs in -ayim, "the" as a prefix, and the one-letter prefixes ו ב ל מ ש.

pages.title: Adjectives & comparisons
pages.summary: Agreement, word order, the little ה that turns a phrase into a sentence, this/that, more/most/too.

pages.title: Smichut (noun + noun)
pages.summary: Bedroom, bus stop, birthday: how Hebrew glues nouns together, and when to just use של.

pages.title: Prepositions with endings
pages.summary: לי, שלי, איתי, אצלי, עליי, ממני, אותי — the forms, את before objects, and which verbs take which preposition.

pages.title: Numbers & time
pages.summary: The two sets of numbers (and which one people really use), prices, telling the time, days of the week.

pages.title: Questions & connectors
pages.summary: Question words, ש־ (that), because / when / if, unreal "if" sentences, and Hebrew double negatives.

pages.title: Must, can, allowed
pages.summary: צריך, יכול, חייב, אמור, אפשר, אסור, מותר, כדאי — with an infinitive, and how to add "who".

pages.title: Roots & binyanim
pages.summary: How three-letter roots plus seven verb patterns build almost every Hebrew verb — and how to spot the pattern.

pages.title: Pa'al
pages.summary: The basic binyan: כָּתַב, כּוֹתֵב, יִכְתּוֹב. Full tables, how people really use it, and the common irregular verbs.

pages.title: Nif'al
pages.summary: Passive and "it happened": נִכְנַס, נִשְׁאַר, נִגְמַר. The doubled letter in the future and the f/p switch.

pages.title: Pi'el
pages.summary: The doubled-middle binyan: דִּיבֵּר, מְדַבֵּר, יְדַבֵּר. Where slang verbs like לְסַמֵּס and לְפַרְגֵּן live.

pages.title: Hif'il
pages.summary: Causative and everyday: הִתְחִיל, הִזְמִין, הֵבִין, הִגִּיעַ. Full tables and the common weak hif'il verbs.

pages.title: Hitpa'el
pages.summary: Reflexive and reciprocal: get dressed, shower, call, get excited — and the ת that jumps places.

pages.title: Pu'al & huf'al
pages.summary: The two passive binyanim — and the everyday adjectives they give you: מסודר, מוזמן, מומלץ, מוכן.

pages.title: Weak roots
pages.summary: Why קונה, גר, נוסע and יושב bend the rules — five root types that explain most "irregular" verbs.

pages.title: Was, will be, had
pages.summary: Past and future of "to be", "I had / I will have" (and why it agrees with the thing), plus "would" and "used to".

pages.title: How people actually talk
pages.summary: שלי instead of suffixes, commands in the future tense, 'עשרים שקל', אצלי, כזה — the gap between the textbook and the street.
